# Features: the PS3 game and the port

What the PS3 version of Killzone 3 does and how far the port reproduces it (section 1), and what the port adds that the PS3 version does not have (section 2). Every status comes from a recorded result in this repository: a screenshot checkpoint, a test, or a dated status note. *Not yet verified* means the code path exists but nothing has exercised it; *works* is only claimed with evidence.

| Status | Meaning | Count |
|---|---|---|
| works | verified in a run | 20 |
| partial | runs, with known gaps | 13 |
| not yet | not reached or not started | 8 |
| not yet verified | present in code, never exercised | 0 |
| declined | will not be done | 0 |
| not applicable | has no equivalent on PC | 2 |

Port-only features: 32 available now, 27 planned.

**Estimated parity with the PS3 version: 65 %** (an estimate: works counts 1, partial 1/2, not yet verified 1/4, not yet 0; declined and not-applicable features are left out).

| Area | Estimated parity | Features |
|---|---|---|
| Campaign and levels | 56 % | 8 |
| Controls | 80 % | 5 |
| Graphics | 81 % | 8 |
| Audio | 75 % | 2 |
| Saves and profile | 100 % | 2 |
| Menus and options | 100 % | 4 |
| Trophies | 50 % | 1 |
| Multiplayer | 20 % | 5 |
| Move and 3D TV | 0 % | 2 |
| Update 1.14 | 50 % | 2 |
| Subtitles and languages | 75 % | 2 |

## 1. Feature parity with the PS3 version

### Campaign and levels

|---|---|---|---|

| Intro movies and opening cinematic (Bink video) | Play on first boot; skippable afterwards | **works**: Full speed; short stalls while a level loads behind a movie | kz3-intro-movie, kz3-opening-cinematic; every movie plays to its end; 2026-10-20 (hand-played session on the main build): the intro and the cinematics play at 28-30 frames/s, the movies' own rate, with their audio; the credits that follow the intro drop to 7-15 frames/s for a few seconds at a time while the level loads behind them, and skipping a cutscene froze the picture for 7 s once |
| Title screen, main menu, attract mode | Main menu with Campaign, Co-op Campaign, Multiplayer, Botzone, Options, Credits; idle returns to the trailer | **works** | kz3-main-menu, kz3-campaign-difficulty, kz3-attract-mode (20-minute soak, no crash) |
| Level 1 (prologue) loads and runs | Loads from Campaign > New Game > difficulty | **partial**: Runs for 10+ minutes; below full speed | kz3-level-geometry, kz3-level-depth-of-field, kz3-level-occluded-coronas; update 1.14 build: a 600 s level run with no game errors; 2026-10-16: levels run at about 16-22 frames/s against the original's 30 (with the shipped pipeline list the busy first minute of chapter 4 runs at about 16.5) |
| In-level play (walk, aim, fire, cover, pause menu) | Gamepad gameplay | **partial**: Playable with a controller at about 16-22 frames/s; audio stutters in levels | A trace run (2026-10-11) shows the scripted stick input reaching the game's movement and view-angle code (UpdateMoveInput, SetViewAngles) at the scripted seconds; 2026-10-13: scripted walk, turn, fire and reload for 670 s in level 2 with 0 game errors (kz3-level2-10min); every level run so far used a scripted pad sequence, a real controller session is still to do; the pause menu was seen once; 2026-10-14: a hand-played session of about 18 minutes with a real controller (Steam, Proton Experimental) moved, aimed, fired, crouched, reloaded, switched weapons and threw grenades in level 202; input responsive for the frame rate (16-22 frames/s); the pause screen's blurred background shows black blocks; 2026-10-14: hand-played with a real controller in Pyrrhus Outskirts (level 202): anti-aircraft guns and dropships destroyed, the vehicle ride finished, the next section reached; pause, quit and Continue all worked; 2026-10-20: a full chapter (level 202) played by hand to its end with an Xbox pad through Steam Input: aiming responsive, controls lag in the first seconds after the level loads, then fine |
| Levels 2 to 9 | Flooded Pyrrhus to Escape from Helghan (level ids 201-208), picked with Campaign > Select Chapter | **partial**: All nine chapters play; level 202 played by hand to its end (2026-10-20), the others not yet; about 16-22 frames/s | kz3-all-levels-load (all nine chapters load and reach their level-start save), kz3-level2, kz3-level5, kz3-level2-10min (670 s of scripted play, 0 game errors); 2026-10-13: eight of the nine chapters ran 5 minutes or more with a picture on the main build; the chapter with level id 202 loads but stays black after its intro cutscene (the world waits on six graphics buffers that are never created); 2026-10-14: all nine chapters load and play 5 minutes each with scripted input on the main build (15.6-19.1 frames/s in the level, no crash or stall); level 202 now draws its scene; level 202 was also played by hand past its vehicle ride; 2026-10-14: all nine chapters ran 5 minutes of scripted play each with a picture, 0 crashes, an autosave in every level, 15.6-19.1 frames/s; 2026-10-20: Pyrrhus Outskirts (level 202) played by hand from its checkpoint to its end on the main build (about 29 minutes, its four cutscenes, the outro into the next chapter, no crash or stall) |
| Full campaign, start to finish | 9 levels, checkpoints, real-time and video cutscenes | **not yet**: Not played start to finish in one go | All nine chapters play for minutes each in separate runs; level 202 was played by hand past its vehicle ride (AA guns and dropships down) to the next section; quitting to the menu and Continue work; 2026-10-20: the first chapter played to its end by hand (level 202, Pyrrhus Outskirts) |

Keyboard/mouse is port-only (section 2) | Xbox (XInput) and SDL2 pads reach the game through the runtime; a scripted pad drives every menu and level test; 2026-10-14: a real controller through Steam Input under Proton played level 202 for about 18 minutes, responsive; the buttons match the game's own Standard control mapping (Options > Controller); 2026-10-20: a DualShock 4 through SDL3 (patch 4010) with Steam Input off and on, and an Xbox Series pad through XInput with Steam Input off, worked by hand (buttons, sticks, triggers, no noticeable delay) |
| Pressure-sensitive buttons | Analog face buttons and shoulder buttons | **not applicable**: The game does not use button pressure | 2026-10-15 (static check of the game binary): the EBOOT imports neither cellPadSetPressMode nor cellPadInfoPressMode, so the game never turns pressure mode on and reads no analog button pressure; nothing to port |
| Rumble | Vibration through the pad | **works**: Works through Steam Input today; rumble on PlayStation and Switch Pro pads without Steam goes through the built-in SDL3 input (SDL3), unconfirmed on real hardware | The game calls the pad actuator interface; 2026-10-14: vibration felt on a real controller through Steam Input under Proton during hand play; patch 4010 adds rumble through SDL3 for pads without Steam (host test only, not yet confirmed on real hardware); 2026-10-20: rumble felt on a DualShock 4 through SDL3 without Steam Input |
| SIXAXIS motion input | Tilt for valves, charges and an optional aim correction | **not yet**: Built in: the pad's own sensors on DualShock 4 and DualSense; not yet confirmed on real hardware. Pads without sensors give rest values | The runtime returns rest values for the motion sensors unless the pad has them: patch 4010 feeds the accelerometer and gyro of DualShock 4, DualSense and Switch Pro pads (through SDL3) into the SENSOR_ON words the game asks for; checked by a host test of the value conversion only, not yet confirmed on real hardware or in a motion section; 2026-10-20: on a real DualShock 4 through SDL3 the runtime reported no motion sensors (sensors no), so the sensor path is still unverified |
| Controller options (schemes, inversion, sensitivity) | Options > Controller | **works**: That the changed values reach in-level aiming was not run (see the in-level play row); on 1.14 the list has an extra SimulView row (Co-Op SimulView, Off), so Wireless Controller is the fifth entry | 2026-10-15 (checked under Proton on the 1.00 and 1.14 builds with a scripted pad): Options > Wireless Controller opens; Control Mapping changes Standard to Alternate (the button diagram follows), Y-Axis changes Normal to Inverted (kz3-options-controller); Advanced Controller Settings opens (X/Y axis, sensitivities, zoom, crouch, stick and shoulder swaps) and Y-Axis Sensitivity changes 30 % to 40 % (kz3-options-advanced-controller, kz3-options-sensitivity) |
| Button prompts (PlayStation glyphs) | Game's own glyphs in hints and menus | **works**: Xbox and keyboard glyph sets are port-only (section 2) | kz3-gamma-screen (the game's own button prompts), kz3-setup-controller-mapping |

### Graphics

| Feature | On the PS3 | In the port | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Resolution and aspect | 1280x720 at 16:9 (the console upscales to the TV) | **works**: Higher internal resolutions, window modes and widescreen options are port-only (section 2) | Render notes: a 1280x720 scene target, as on the PS3; the port opens a 1280x720 window by default (display modes built in patch 2095; checked by hand under Proton at 1920x1080 on 2026-10-21 (windowed to borderless with Alt+Enter, picture good), other shapes only in test runs) |
| Frame rate | 30 frames/s target, vertical sync | **partial**: Menus at 30 frames/s; the levels at about 16-22 (target 30); speed is the current blocker | Menus hold the game's own 30 frames/s (kz3-main-menu, kz3-main-menu-texture-gamma); a busy level window runs at about 22-23 frames/s on the test machine (Frozen Shores, 131-180 s after launch, means of alternated runs on 2026-10-27, in-level figure; the slowest 1 % of frames about 13-14 frames/s); RPCS3 holds 30 on the same scene and machine; the CPU side (main thread and SPU job code) is the limit, the GPU needs 12-14 ms per frame; the port presents with vertical sync on by default (a setting: Options > Display > VSync); 2026-10-20 hand play on the main build: intro and cutscenes 28-30 frames/s, level 202 about 16-20 |
| Deferred lighting, sun shadows, depth of field, post effects | The game's deferred renderer with an SPU post-processing chain | **partial** | kz3-level-depth-of-field (lighting, shadows, depth of field), kz3-level-effects-layer (particles, light shafts); open: menu background haze darker than the reference (kz3-main-menu-texture-gamma), soft particles |
| Anti-aliasing (MLAA on the SPUs) | Morphological AA as an SPU post job | **partial**: A host FXAA pass is the planned replacement at higher resolutions (section 2) | The SPU MLAA job runs in the port (it is the most expensive SPU job); image quality against the reference not compared |
| Occlusion of light coronas | Hidden behind geometry | **works** | kz3-level-occluded-coronas (conditional rendering with occlusion queries) |
| Menu text and fonts | The game's glyph renderer | **works** | kz3-setup-controller-mapping (all menu text correct), kz3-language-menu-live-draw |
| In-level HUD (ammo, crosshair, objective text) | The game's HUD layer over the level | **works**: Drawn as on the PS3 (the dark SELECT square in hints is the game's own glyph) | HUD text in kz3-level-geometry; the 2026-10-11 gameplay runs show no ammo counter and only a faint crosshair (under investigation); 2026-10-14 hand play: ammo counter, grenades, crosshair, objective banner and hints drawn |
| Brightness (gamma) setting | First-run and options page | **works**: A level scene not checked yet | 2026-10-15 (patch 2070, runs r66-gm6/gm8/gm9): the game's cellVideoOutSetGamma value is applied at scan-out; on Options > Display > Brightness the picture darkens and brightens with the slider (mean luma 9.3 -> 7.9 / 11.3) and the value is restored after a restart; at the default 1.0 nothing changes |

## 2. Features the PS3 version does not have

Non-original features are opt-in where they change gameplay; display and input improvements may be on by default. Each is marked `ENHANCEMENT:` in the source. The switch column names the environment variable that controls the feature where one exists (the settings page will expose them).

### Available now

| Feature | State | Default | Switch, notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Archive reads by the port's own file layer | available | on | KZ3_PSARC_VFS=0 turns it off. Same files and bytes as the game's own archive reader; no gameplay change; faster loading |
| Scheduler deadlock breaker | available | on (2 s) | KZ3_FIBER_DEADLOCK=<seconds>, 0 = report only. Resumes one stalled entity update when every slot waits on a flag nobody can set; a workaround for a state the original never reaches |
| Log files, crash reports and an error notice | available | on | KZ3_LOG=tag:level, KZ3_LOG_LEVEL, KZ3_NO_ERROR_BOX=1. Timestamped logs next to the exe (last 10 kept), a crash file plus minidump on a host crash, and a notice in the game's menu style (kz3-error-notice) |
| Asynchronous shader builds | available | off (opt-in) | LD_PSO_ASYNC=1, LD_PSO_ASYNC_THREADS=<n> (default 3). The renderer does not stall while a missing shader is built; opt-in until it is measured on more runs. The shipped pipeline list (next row) is on by default and does not need this switch |
| Shipped pipeline list: shaders build in the background while a level loads | available | on | LD_PSO_TEMPLATE=0 turns it off. Measured on chapter 4 (2026-10-16): the busy first minute of a first visit runs at about 16.5 frames/s with little stutter, and a cold start builds 8-26 pipelines on the render thread (under 1.3 s). A file of hashes and render state only, no game code; it covers the 8 chapters it was recorded on, and the shader cache carries over between sessions |
| Window modes and scaling (windowed, borderless, fullscreen, Alt+Enter, resizable, DPI aware) | available | on | Three modes (windowed, borderless, exclusive fullscreen as a setting), Alt+Enter, resizable window, Fit/Stretch and Bilinear/Nearest, Options > Display rows; host-tested and checked by hand under Proton at 1920x1080 (2026-10-21); DPI awareness not done |
| Rebindable controls (every action, primary and secondary key, conflict warning, reset; saved to a local config file) | available | on | Keyboard page in the game's Options menus and keybinds.ini in the data folder; on-screen prompts show the bound keys when the keyboard is in use (pad glyphs again on a pad press); keyboard play confirmed by hand (2026-10-14); gamepad remap later |
| Button prompts that follow the device in use (PlayStation, Xbox, keyboard/mouse), XInput rumble | available | auto | Glyphs drawn by the port in the game's own style; chosen on Options > Controls > Advanced Settings > Layout and Prompts |
| Discord Rich Presence: “Playing Killzone 3” with the current chapter | available | off (opt-in) | Opt-in: Options > Display > Discord status, or the Start menu entry “Discord status on or off” (both saved as discord_presence in kz3.ini), through the local Discord app on your PC; nothing is sent when it is off. Built, host-tested (tools/net/test_discord.sh) and checked under Proton without the Discord app; the live check against the Discord app is still being tested |
| Exit Game in the main menu (with a confirm prompt) | available | on | EXIT GAME under CREDITS with the game's own confirm dialog; a clean exit (dialog text in English only) |
| Quit to desktop from the pause menu (with a confirm prompt) | available | on | QUIT TO DESKTOP under the game's Quit row in the campaign pause menu, with the game's own quit dialog; checked in the campaign, the multiplayer pause menu not yet |
| The window title and the process name in Task Manager read Project Helghast, with the port's icon | available | on | Version info, icon and manifest in the exe; the title bar shows no debug numbers (KZ3_TITLE_STATS=1 adds them) |
| Chinese, Korean, Russian and Japanese text from your own PS3 system fonts or bundled open fonts | available | on when no system font is installed | With the player's own PS3 system fonts (a folder from their firmware install); the bundled open-font fallback covers Latin and Cyrillic so far |
| Game language follows your Windows language (override with KZ3_LANG) | available | on | A fresh profile starts in your Windows language when the disc has it; the in-game language list still changes it |

| Keyboard binds by key position (WASD stays put on AZERTY, QWERTZ, Dvorak) | available | on | The Keyboard page shows your layout's key names |
| Native mouse look on foot, on by default (KZ3_MOUSE_LOOK=0 or kz3.ini mouse_look = 0 turns it off): raw mouse counts into the game's own look, PC-style sensitivity in degrees per count (kz3.ini [input] mouse_sensitivity, default 2.5 x 0.022 degrees; mouse_ads_sensitivity; mouse_invert_y), scaled by the weapon's zoom; every count is shown on the view at once (KZ3_MOUSE_LATCH=0 switches the view to the game's own timing); no stick dead zone, acceleration or smoothing; mouse movement made while menus, pauses or loading screens are up is dropped instead of turning the view later | available | on | Scripted counts verified within 0.15 degrees; conversion and drop rule host-tested; the default sensitivity is not hand-checked; mounted guns (the turret ride in the fourth chapter) follow the mouse within the gun's own range with the simulation's look timing (checked in one scripted run); vehicles and turning off aim assist are not done; render-rate fill (patch 2116, default on): counts-to-view about 0 ms, aim (where shots go) on the 30 Hz clock about 35 ms behind the view; hand check pending |

Start-menu entries Open saves folder / Move saves and settings |
| Gameplay view at the window's aspect (Hor+ on ultrawide, Vert+ on 16:10) | available | on | KZ3_ASPECT=16:9 (or off) keeps the PS3 camera. Checked under Proton at 16:10, 16:9 and 21:9 in Frozen Shores; HUD, menus, subtitles and movies stay 16:9 and centred (see the HUD row) and world markers project with the same view; the game still draws at 1280x720 |
| VSync on or off (display.ini vsync = on\|off, or Options > Display > VSync); with it off, frames may tear where the system allows it; the game's own 60 Hz clock is unchanged | available | on | Both settings checked under Proton (the log shows the setting and that tearing is allowed); tearing not yet checked by eye; VRR, a frame limiter and a low-latency mode are still planned |
| Options > Mouse page: mouse sensitivity, zoomed-in sensitivity and invert Y, applied at once and saved | available | - | Checked under Proton: values applied, saved and read back when the page is opened again |
| Esc goes back in menus on the keyboard, as Circle does on a pad (Backspace still works) | available | on | Checked under Proton with scripted keys |
| Frame rate limit 30, 60 or 120 (Options > Display > Frame rate limit, display.ini fps_limit); above 30 a warning says game logic tied to the frame rate may misbehave | available | on | Default 30, the game's own; the limit only raises the cap, the levels still run at about 16-22 frames/s |
| Field of view setting for the campaign and co-op (Options > Display > Field of view, Default or 70-110; display.ini fov); aiming down sights stays relative | available | opt-in | Default keeps the game's own; off in every multiplayer mode |
| Keyboard and mouse count as their own controller while a pad is connected, so one pad plus the keyboard can play split-screen co-op; a single player on pad and keyboard plays as before | available | default on | Mouse look still turns the first player's view (planned); checked with scripted input, not yet by hand |
| Bloom strength setting (Options > Display > Bloom, 0-100 % in steps of 10; display.ini bloom); 100 is the game's own look, 0 removes the glow | available | 100 | Row, saved value and the scaled strength checked under Proton in K4 (frames at 100, 50 and 0 compared; the effect is modest in that scene); other levels and 1.00 not run |
| Pad layouts: the game's own scheme by default, a Modern preset, or a Custom layout per action (33 groups, swap on conflict, copy Default or Modern, keybinds.ini [pad actions]); Options > Controls > Advanced Settings > Layout and Prompts page | available | opt-in (the game's own layout is the default) | The Modern preset changes gameplay buttons only (on foot), applied inside the game's own action table; menus keep Cross to confirm and Circle to go back, checked in the Options screens in one run. The Modern preset follows the Killzone Shadow Fall layout (fire R2, aim L2, grenade R1, reload Square, jump Cross); in one level fire, reload, jump and aim worked on the new buttons (2026-10-27); Modern keeps Use on Circle and its controller picture shows no L1 line; Use at a use prompt is not checked. Custom: checked on screen only; not played in a level, real-pad capture unchecked. The Layout and Prompts page has row descriptions and a picture per layout and the game's controller page shows the Xbox and keyboard prompt sets. Its full effect in a level is not yet confirmed |
| Option pages that match the game: descriptions for the port's rows in the game's tooltip panel, the Display list scrolling inside the game's list area, Reset to defaults covering the port's rows, and a menu pointer in the game's colours | available | on | Checked under Proton by screenshot; the pointer and the menu sounds still need a check by hand |
| HUD, menus, subtitles and movies stay 16:9 and centred on wide, ultrawide and 16:10 screens while the 3D view fills the window (display.ini hud_169; no Options row yet) | available | default on | Checked at 32:9, 21:9, 16:10 and 16:9 in Frozen Shores; world markers (objective markers, name tags) project with the 16:9 view (bot name tags seen on target in Botzone at 32:9); the Botzone HUD shows one minimap at 16:9 and 32:9 in scripted runs; objective markers on screen not yet seen |
| Opt-in crash reports to the project's error tracker | available | off | Installer Advanced page or the Start menu's “Crash reports on or off”. Sent by the launcher after a crash when you opt in: one report per session (reason, stack addresses, the last 200 log lines with user, machine, address, online-id and folder names removed), never the minidump. Host test test_crash_report.py; not yet sent to the real tracker from a release build |

### Planned

| Feature | State | Default | Switch, notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Internal resolution scale (720p, 1080p, 1440p, 4K, match window) | planned | on where it looks right | Host render targets scaled while the game keeps its 1280x720 view |
| Host anti-aliasing (FXAA) in place of SPU MLAA | planned | on at scaled resolutions | KZ3_HOST_AA=fxaa or off. The pass exists (patch 2023) and only runs once the port skips the SPU MLAA job, which is not active yet |
| Widescreen: 16:10 and 4:3 bars, ultrawide Hor+ field of view | planned | bars on; ultrawide opt-in | Gameplay view at the window aspect and the HUD, menus, subtitles and movies kept 16:9 and centred are built (see Available now); not done: 4:3 and 16:10 bars as an option and a HUD anchored to the screen edges |
| VRR, frame limiter, low-latency mode | planned | - | The game's own 60 Hz clock stays fixed whatever the monitor |
| 60 frames/s and above | planned | off where it changes gameplay | The game is paced from its vblank; some elements misbehave at higher rates |
| Keyboard and mouse with native mouse aim | planned | on when a mouse or keyboard is used | Raw mouse deltas into the game's view, not a fake stick. On foot it is available now and on by default, with the cursor hidden and locked to the window (see “Native mouse look” and “Cursor hiding and mouse lock” below); mounted guns follow the mouse within the gun's range (one scripted run); vehicles and aim assist are planned |
| Aim assist as a setting | planned | off on mouse and keyboard, on with a gamepad | Decided 2026-10-07 |
| Aim response (lighter stick smoothing and acceleration) as a setting | planned | original response by default (opt-in) | Community request 2026-10-15 |
| Motion-sensor sections on the stick by default; gyro pass-through for pads that have one | planned | stick when the pad has no gyro | Gyro pass-through itself is coded (patch 4010, built in; unconfirmed on real hardware); the stick default and the opt-in setting are still to do |
| PC settings page in the game's own menu style | planned | - | Options > Display (modes, scaling, VSync) and Options > Mouse exist; resolution and anti-aliasing are still planned |
| Native Linux build | planned | - | No Proton needed; after the Windows build plays the campaign |
| Native macOS build (Apple silicon) | planned | - | Wanted backlog (2026-10-15); after the native Linux build |
| Native upgrade path toward a full decompilation | planned | - | Wanted backlog (2026-10-15); after feature parity and VR: native renderer, native SPU jobs, then rewritten game code |
| Android (ARM64) build | planned | - | Late stage, after the Windows and Linux builds and once the desktop build has about 2x speed headroom; the player builds the APK on their PC from their own game files |
| Better than the PS3: steadier frame rate, lower input lag, shorter loads, optional 60 fps | planned | steadiness on; 60 fps opt-in | After the port matches the console; each improvement measured against the console's figures and switchable |
| Ray-traced sun shadows, then ambient occlusion and reflections | planned | off | KZ3_RT_SHADOWS=1 (planned). Geometry capture spike passed (patch 2024); after the campaign runs at speed |
| Mod support (data mods as folders over the game's archive; code mods later) | planned | off (no mods = the game as shipped) | Late stage (decided 2026-10-09) |
| Stereoscopic 3D output (side by side, top and bottom) from the game's own 3D mode | planned | off | Wanted backlog (2026-10-15); not before the campaign is playable |
| VR (SteamVR headsets) | planned | off | Wanted backlog (2026-10-08); not before the campaign is playable |
| PlayStation Move and Sharpshooter (psmoveapi; camera tracking or motion-sensor pointer) | planned | off | Wanted backlog (2026-10-15); not before the campaign is playable |
| Renderer choice (Direct3D 12, Vulkan or OpenGL, picked in the installer) | planned | Direct3D 12 | Goal recorded; scoped after the campaign renders correctly on Direct3D 12 |
| Temporal anti-aliasing and upscaling (TAA, DLAA, DLSS, FSR): the game renders no motion vectors, so camera-only vectors first, character ghosting measured | planned | Backlog after parity; not started | SMAA/FXAA and resolution scale cover image quality until then |
| Saves in the PS3's own format: copy a save between the port, RPCS3 and a PS3 | planned | - | The port writes a real PARAM.SFO so its save folder loads in RPCS3; 2026-10-14: the port writes PARAM.SFO as a binary PSF (checked by a host test with an independent reader, and written by a real checkpoint save in a hand-played session); older text files still load; opening a port save in RPCS3 or on a console is untested |

| In-game voice chat for multiplayer and the online co-op campaign (microphone and headset on the PC; online only when the player picks it) | planned | opt-in | Wanted backlog (2026-10-27); after online play and the online co-op campaign |
